# Cache probe, 2026-10-21

`bun scripts/cache-probe.ts --model <ref> --turns 20 --runs 3`, from a cloud session through OpenCode Go (key added by the egress proxy). Each run is a fresh session that reads 19 small files one per turn, then answers. Prompts are small (about 700 to 2,300 tokens), so the hit ratio is capped by how much each turn adds; prefix reuse is the share of what a perfect cache could serve that the provider actually served.

| Model (wire) | Hit after first request, mean (min to max) | Prefix reuse, mean (min to max) | Misses and cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Haiku 5.5 via Go (Anthropic Messages) | 95.8% (95.8 to 95.8) | 100% (100 to 100) | none; each read lands about 2 tokens short of the previous input |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash via Go (Chat Completions) | 88.7% (87.0 to 90.8) | 97.7% (95.7 to 100) | provider: reads lag one 128-token block on some turns, and one read per run fell back to 640 tokens |
| beam-free via Go (Chat Completions) | 79.2% (68.2 to 85.5) | 89.8% (78.0 to 95.9) | provider: reads dropped to 0 or a short prefix with an unchanged request prefix |

All 9 runs ended `success`. In every run `systemHash` and `toolsHash` stayed constant and each request extended the previous one, so no miss traces to cedia.

Claude through the Anthropic API directly is measured below, under "Anthropic API direct". Grok 4.7 via Go (Responses) was checked with one 2-turn session: tool call, reasoning replay and cache read all worked.

Readings:
- DeepSeek caches in 128-token blocks. Anthropic reads stop a few tokens short at the turn boundary. `cacheBlockTokens` in the catalog encodes both, so the probe does not count block rounding as a miss.
- The 90% hit target is reachable on Haiku. On DeepSeek it depends on prompt size; real sessions carry a larger system prompt and larger tool results, which raises the ratio. Re-measure with the stage 2 system prompt.

## Realistic prompt size

Same probe with `--context SPEC.md --context AGENTS.md` (system prompt about 19,900 characters, roughly 5k tokens), closer to a real session:

| Model (wire) | Hit after first request | Prefix reuse | Misses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Haiku 5.5 via Go (Anthropic Messages) | 99.2% (99.2 to 99.2) | 100% | 0 in 3 runs |

Claude Code's `/usage` line reports the same quantity ("share of input tokens served from cache"); its system prompt and tools are larger still, so it rounds to 100%.

## Anthropic API direct

Same `--context SPEC.md --context AGENTS.md` probe, `--model anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`, key read from `CEDIA_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`:

| Model (wire) | Hit after first request | Prefix reuse | Whole session, first request included | Misses | Cost, 3 runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Haiku 5.5 via Anthropic API | 99.2% (99.24 to 99.25) | 100% | 94.6% run 1, 99.2% runs 2 and 3 | 0 in 3 runs | $0.0089 |

All 3 runs ended `success` with 20 requests each.

Readings:
- Direct and Go give the same hit ratio, so Go adds no cache loss for Claude.
- The ceiling is the new turn, not the cache: each request writes 66 to 116 new tokens (the last tool call and its result) on top of about 8.6k to 9.9k read tokens, which caps this probe near 99.2%. Claude Code shows 100% because its prompt is larger and the line rounds.
- Run 1 wrote the 8.6k-token prefix cold. Runs 2 and 3 read 8,442 tokens of it on their first request, written by the previous run: system prompt and tools are byte-identical across sessions, and the read stops at the preamble, which names the per-run temp directory.
